key_moments.speaker: Priya Nair
key_moments.summary: Priya admits ACME's own team used to let webinar leads sit for days despite good attendance, framing the session as lessons from doing it wrong.

key_moments.speaker: Daniel Kim
key_moments.summary: Daniel reveals the 3.2x reply rate stat for 4-hour follow-up vs next-day, which was the number that secured budget for their process rebuild.

key_moments.speaker: Sara Alvarez
key_moments.summary: Sara shares the multi-threading insight: accounts with 3+ attendees convert to opportunity at nearly double the rate of single-attendee accounts.

key_moments.speaker: Sara Alvarez
key_moments.summary: Sara introduces the internal routing speed problem, revealing that cutting routing delay from 18 hours to under 2 hours lifted opportunity creation by 41%.

key_moments.speaker: Daniel Kim
key_moments.summary: Daniel reveals no-show follow-up emails with a 3-bullet summary outperform attendee follow-ups in click-through rate in 6 of the last 8 webinars.

key_moments.speaker: Sara Alvarez
key_moments.summary: Sara shares the segmentation lift data: moving from blanket sends to three-way segmentation tripled click-through rates from ~6% to ~17%.

key_moments.speaker: Daniel Kim
key_moments.summary: Daniel discloses that repurposed content generates 2.4x the pipeline-influenced touches of the original live session across six events.

key_moments.speaker: Sara Alvarez
key_moments.summary: Sara states the fully-attributed ROI range of 11-14x on fully-loaded event cost within two quarters, counting both direct and repurposed-content-sourced pipeline.

key_moments.speaker: Sara Alvarez
key_moments.summary: Sara delivers the line 'Attribution is the mirror, not the engine,' reframing attribution as measurement rather than a value-creation lever.

key_moments.speaker: Daniel Kim
key_moments.summary: Daniel identifies the single biggest mistake: treating every attendee identically with one email and send time regardless of engagement depth.

quotes.speaker: Priya Nair
quotes.quote: for years our own team ran webinars, got great attendance, felt good about ourselves, and then just... let the leads sit. Like, sit for days.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: accounts with three or more attendees on the same webinar convert to opportunity at almost double the rate of single-attendee accounts. Multi-threading basically happens by accident at a webinar and most teams don't even notice it's happening.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Kim
quotes.quote: the person just spent an hour thinking about your topic, it's fresh, they might still have the tab open. A day later they're back in their actual job, dealing with their actual fires, and your webinar is a distant memory competing with forty other emails in their inbox.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: when we cut the internal routing delay from an average of about eighteen hours down to under two hours, our webinar-sourced opportunity creation rate went up by forty-one percent over the following quarter. Same leads, same list quality, just faster internal handoff.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: even an imperfect score beats no score. The alternative most teams have is literally alphabetical order or whoever registered first gets called first, which has zero correlation with actual interest.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: The speaker thank-you — especially when it's an external speaker like Daniel today, or like me — should not just be a generic 'thanks for joining.' It should include an actual performance snapshot.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: A lot of this is small details, honestly, that's kind of the theme of the whole talk. None of these individually feel revolutionary, it's the compounding of a dozen small correct decisions instead of a dozen small default ones.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: Repurposing without attribution is just content marketing theater.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Kim
quotes.quote: If you try to summarize the whole event in every post you get ten posts that all feel like the same press release.

quotes.speaker: Daniel Kim
quotes.quote: Attribution doesn't create value, it just measures value that was created by doing the earlier steps well.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: Attribution is the mirror, not the engine.

quotes.speaker: Sara Alvarez
quotes.quote: doing the work of timing and segmentation well, and then not tagging any of it, so three months later nobody can prove any of it mattered and the whole program gets deprioritized in the next budget cycle for something that looks flashier but actually performs worse. Tag everything, from day one, even if the tracking feels tedious in the moment.

data_points.speaker: Daniel Kim
data_points.context: Follow-up within 4 hours lifts reply rate 3.2x compared to next-day follow-up; this stat secured budget for the process rebuild.

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Accounts with 3+ attendees on the same webinar convert to opportunity at nearly double the rate of single-attendee accounts.

data_points.speaker: Daniel Kim
data_points.context: Follow-up within 1 hour has best reply rates; within 4 hours still 3.2x vs next-day; by 24 hours drops to 1.4x; by 48 hours at baseline (no lift vs 96 hours).

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Cutting internal routing delay from ~18 hours average to under 2 hours increased webinar-sourced opportunity creation by 41% over the following quarter with same leads and list quality.

data_points.speaker: Daniel Kim
data_points.context: No-show follow-up email (recording + 3-bullet summary) achieved better click-through rate than attendee follow-up in 6 of the last 8 webinars.

data_points.speaker: Daniel Kim
data_points.context: Stat-led subject line outperformed speaker-name-led subject line by approximately 14 percentage points in open rate on attendee thank-you send.

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Moving from single blanket post-webinar email to three-way segmentation (attendee, no-show, speaker) with role-based variants tripled overall click-through rate across the full post-event send.

data_points.speaker: Daniel Kim
data_points.context: Repurposed content (blog, social, infographic) from a single 60-minute webinar generated 2.4x the pipeline-influenced touches of the original live session, averaged across the last 6 events.

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Quote posts (single bold quote + speaker name) get approximately 40% higher engagement than summary-style posts in their testing.

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Attendees who received segmented follow-up within the critical window reached MQL status about 60% faster (measured in days) than attendees who got generic delayed follow-up.

data_points.speaker: Sara Alvarez
data_points.context: Across fully-attributed events at Meridian, return on fully-loaded event cost (including follow-up and repurposing effort) ranges 11-14x within two quarters, counting both direct attendee pipeline and secondary pipeline from repurposed content.
